### Basic Film/Documentary Information

* **Title**: 60 Minutes
* **Episode # & Title (if applicable)**: 1.3. 28 Years
* **Director(s)**: Information Unavailable
* **Release Year**: Circa 2011 (Segment covered events from 2010-2011)
* **Production Company(ies)**: CBS News
* **Format**: TV news magazine segment
* **Focus/Theme**: DNA exoneration after decades of imprisonment; Eyewitness misidentification
* **Key Statistics/Information**: Profiled one of the longest-serving US exonerees at the time (30 years); Noted 41 DNA exonerations in Texas (2001-2011).

### Wrongfully Convicted Individuals Featured

* **Name**: Cornelius Dupree Jr.
    * **Case Location**: Dallas, Texas, USA
    * **Conviction Year**: 1980
    * **Exoneration Year**: January 2011 (Paroled July 2010)
    * **Crime Convicted Of**: Aggravated Robbery (stemming from a 1979 rape/carjacking incident; never tried for rape)
    * **Sentence**: 75 years
    * **Time Served**: 30 years
    * **Contributing Factors**: Eyewitness misidentification (one victim identified him, another did not); DNA later excluded him.
    * **Legal Status**: Exonerated by DNA evidence
    * **Organizations Involved**: Innocence Project; Dallas County District Attorney's Conviction Integrity Unit.

### Film/Documentary Research Notes

* **Key Quotes/Moments**:
    * Cornelius Dupree: "words really won't make up for what I lost... I lost both my parents uh I just feel that you know the system need to be fixed..."
    * Highlighting that Dupree refused parole because it required admitting guilt/registering as a sex offender.
* **Systemic Issues Identified**: Eyewitness misidentification; Lengthy imprisonment before exoneration; Personal toll of wrongful conviction (loss of family); Conditions attached to parole eligibility.
* **Policy Recommendations/Calls to Action**: Dupree calls for systemic fixes to prevent similar cases.
* **Additional Resources**:
    * [Cornelius Dupree - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelius_Dupree)
    * [Innocence Project Case Profile](https://innocenceproject.org/) (Specific Dupree link not in results, but mentioned)
